clue.text: Will is old-fashioned enough about a large figure

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps round the other here

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large figure

explanation.surface: A will drafted in quaint language mentions a big sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts D, the Roman 500, inside ENOW, the old form of enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To will property to someone is to bestow it on them, a synonym.

clue.text: Work out the money allowed for a little shot

parts.note: PE, physical education, is a workout at school
L is the abbreviation for pound, the British money (from Latin libra)
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Someone calculates a cash allowance for a small dram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like a verb meaning calculate; it is PE, physical exercise. L stands for pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small ball of lead fired from a shotgun, a piece of small shot.

clue.text: Some retired reverential holy man-a monk

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some of something
pi is crossword shorthand for pious, reverential
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A devout holy man who has withdrawn from the world is a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' is the reversal signal on 'Some'; PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious, so it stands for 'reverential'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappists are a Cistercian order known for strict silence, so one of them is a monastic brother.

clue.text: Perfume that can cause an adverse reaction?

definitions.text: that can cause an adverse reaction?

explanation.surface: A scent that might bring on an allergic response.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as the verb stressed on the second syllable, to make angry; an angry response is an adverse reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Burned resin gives a fragrant smoke, a scent; as a verb it means to enrage, provoking a hostile response.

clue.text: Don't give date of birth for such insurance

definitions.text: Don't give date of birth for such insurance

parts.words: Don't give date of birth for such insurance
parts.note: split the word into two: hide how old you are, the instruction an insurance form seems to give

explanation.surface: Advice to withhold your birth date when buying a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy provides, and read in two parts it means concealing your years.

clue.text: Supporters stand here free

indicators.note: free signals the letters of stand here are loosed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Followers are invited to stand in this spot at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the nine letters of STAND HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers who stick to a cause, its backers.

clue.text: Winning over the listener in the finish

indicators.note: in places the listener inside the word for the finish

parts.note: an ending is the finish
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A runner charms the crowd as they cross the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Winning over' is a verb here, so it matches the -ing form of the answer used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearing someone, as a verb, means making yourself dear to them, charming them.

clue.text: Capital that's tied up?

parts.note: money locked into fixed-term securities, and also things that tie up, like ropes or fetters

explanation.surface: Money that cannot be spent because it is locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Government securities lock capital away for a term, and fetters tie people up.

clue.text: There's some incentive in this pursuit

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words this pursuit

explanation.surface: This activity offers some motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across thiS PURsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a goad or stimulus, from the spike on a rider's heel.

clue.text: Wood's holding everybody back, being a total failure

indicators.note: holding means the wood contains the other piece

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: back means the word for everybody is turned round

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A forest restrains everyone, a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word for everybody round, and 'holding' says the wood goes around it. 'being' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a complete breakdown, a total failure.

clue.text: A copper once used by the cook

explanation.surface: An old policeman found working in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers were early London police, named after Sir Robert Peel; 'copper' is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a police constable after Robert Peel; also a kitchen tool for removing vegetable skins.

clue.text: Case for a seamstress in perpetuity

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word perpetuity

explanation.surface: A sewing kit that lasts for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside perpETUIty.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental needle case.

clue.text: Barely moved-or moved very fast!

explanation.surface: Someone moved naked, or else sped by.
explanation.walkthrough: To streak is to run naked through a public place; it also means to move at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Running nude in public is streaking; so is darting along like lightning.

clue.text: The flight one's tried to switch

indicators.note: to switch signals the letters are changed round into a new order

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An escape route someone has attempted to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch' rearranges ONES and TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is abandoning one's post, running away from it as in fleeing.

clue.text: Cache discovered in South-east Mediterranean island

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A hoard turns up in the south-east of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cache' looks like a noun, a hoard; here it is the verb to hide. 'discovered in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to hide it, and to secrete it is to conceal it.

clue.text: He understands his property is to be sold

definitions.text: his property is to be sold

explanation.surface: A man grasps that his house is going on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: To realise means both to understand and to sell property for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: One who grasps a fact, and one who converts assets into money by selling them.

clue.text: Delayed acquiring further equipment for the new baby

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for delayed takes in the other piece

parts.note: late means delayed
yet means further or still more, as in yet another

explanation.surface: Someone held up buys more gear for a newborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' is the container signal: the word for delayed takes in the word for further.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a complete set of clothes and bedding for a newborn infant.

clue.text: Having no following nevertheless

explanation.surface: Someone without supporters, but still.
explanation.walkthrough: Being behind everyone means nobody follows you; the phrase also means in spite of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming behind everybody leaves no one behind you; the phrase also means despite that.

clue.text: The carrier negotiating a treaty

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working the letters of a treaty into a new form

explanation.surface: A courier taking part in treaty talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiating' rearranges A TREATY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray for tea things is used to carry cups and pot.

clue.text: Unfortunately die as vet gives a calming drug

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of die as vet are jumbled

explanation.surface: An animal dies as a vet administers a tranquilliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges DIE AS VET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a tranquilliser that soothes the nerves.

clue.text: The unit returning dry will finds sweets the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

indicators.note: returning means the word for dry comes back to front

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: A dry will is found to bring desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' is the reversal signal for the French wine term for dry; 'will finds' and 'the answer' are filler links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are frozen desserts, sweet courses.

clue.text: Make the point another time

parts.note: taken as written
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Argue your case at some other moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, N for north.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means at that other moment, not now.

clue.text: It's all off!

parts.note: a stage direction telling everyone to leave the stage, not a cancellation

explanation.surface: An announcement that an event is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction means they go out, sending the whole cast offstage.

clue.text: Many were in debt, so cut down

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many
owed means were in debt

explanation.surface: Lots of people in arrears, so spending was slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives M, the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass or corn that has been mown has been cut down with a scythe or mower.

clue.text: A step bringing direst trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of direst are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: One move that leads to the worst possible mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DIREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long pace when walking.

clue.text: Attacked, but got to work

explanation.surface: Someone was set upon, but then got busy.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase means rounded on someone; it also means switched on, started working.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounding on someone is attacking; a machine switched on has been set working.

clue.text: Scowl when let down

explanation.surface: Frowning when disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming with 'flower', the word means to frown; rhyming with 'slower', to let down.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown darkly; and to drop something by rope.

clue.text: European project accepted by youth with little hesitation

indicators.note: accepted by means the project is taken inside the word for youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a plan is a project
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A young man takes on a scheme with barely a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' says the project sits inside the youth; 'with' joins on the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander lives in Lapland, in northern Scandinavia, so is from Europe.
